_: Which visual belongs on which pitch slide. This is the reusable part: the recipe, the data it needs, and what to render when the project hasn't got that data yet. build.cjs reads it; a slide whose data is missing renders the fallback and a 'verify' footer rather than a made-up number.

cover.purpose: Name plus the one line you want repeated back.
cover.done: Someone who missed the title can still say what you do.
cover.note: Type only. A visual here competes with the line you want them to hear.

problem.purpose: The pain, dated and specific — not a category.
problem.done: A listener has personally felt it.
problem.why: The problem is temporal — something decays and you notice too late. A timeline shows the gap between the two.

insight.purpose: The non-obvious thing you know that others don't.
insight.done: It is not a feature, and a competitor would argue with it.
insight.why: An insight is almost always 'X is handled, Y is not'. Two panels make the asymmetry visible.

solution.purpose: What you built, in three verbs.
solution.done: No adjectives survive on the slide.
solution.why: Three to four verbs. Cards, not a paragraph.

whynow.purpose: Why this is buildable now and wasn't two years ago.
whynow.done: Every mark is a real shift, not a trend word.
whynow.why: Why-now is a sequence of enabling shifts. Dated marks, no invented figures.

product.purpose: The pipeline, one hand-off per arrow.
product.done: It asks the user to change no habits.
product.why: Pipeline left to right, one arrow per hand-off. Screenshot goes on the NEXT slide, not here.

market.done: Every term is counted and cited, none borrowed.
market.why: Bottom-up multiplication, shown as the arithmetic. A top-down borrowed TAM gets you caught.
market.fallback: em dashes in every cell plus an 'unsourced' footer

competition.purpose: Two axes that leave you alone in one corner.
competition.done: The axes are true even if a rival drew them.
competition.why: Axes are the argument. Pick the two that put you alone in one corner and are still true.

model.purpose: Who pays, how much, per what.
model.done: It names the buyer, not the user.
model.note: One line. A pricing diagram before a pilot is theatre.

traction.purpose: Only what you have actually measured.
traction.done: Every number can be reproduced live.
traction.why: Only for numbers actually measured. No data = one honest sentence instead.
traction.fallback: big-number slide plus 'nothing else is true yet'

team.done: The why-us line would be false for any other team.
team.why: One card per person, role first. Headshots only if they exist as real files.

vision.purpose: The wedge expanding into a company.
vision.done: It is a company, not a bigger feature.
vision.why: A wedge expanding outward. Innermost ring is what you sell today.

ask.purpose: What you want, and the biggest risk named first.
ask.done: The risk is on the slide before they ask it.
ask.note: The ask and the biggest risk. No diagram.

cannot_generate.product_screenshot: Must be captured from the running project — see capture.sh. Uploaded as a deck asset and referenced as /_blob/<id>; it is the one visual that does NOT live inside the slide file.
cannot_generate.photos: Team photos, venue shots, anything real. Supply the file; never generate a stand-in that reads as real.
cannot_generate.logos: Customer or partner logos. Only ones you have permission to show.

timeline.use: Something decaying, or a sequence of enabling shifts. `hot` paints one mark in the risk color.

split.use: An asymmetry — one side handled, the other not. Right panel reads as the problem.

flow.use: A pipeline or a hand-off chain, 2-4 stages. Arrows between, themed.

stack.use: Bottom-up multiplication shown as the arithmetic itself. The total is outlined in the accent.

bars.use: Measured numbers only. `pct` drives bar width, `value` is the printed figure.

quadrant.use: Positioning map. x and y are 0-1 fractions; `hot` is you.

rings.use: A wedge expanding. layers[0] is what you sell today and draws filled; up to 4.
